description_en: System Operationalization Rubric v1 for supply-chain bottleneck, pricing power, and operating leverage identification. This is an engineering research specification, not an official Serenity formula, calibrated explosion probability, or personalized investment recommendation.
description_zh_TW: 系統化操作評分標準 v1，用於供應鏈結構性瓶頸、定價權與營運槓桿識別。此為工程研究規格，並非 Serenity 本人官方公式、校準之爆發機率或個人化投資建議。

dependency_criticality.description: Functional necessity of component/process in system architecture; system cannot function or scale without it.

anchors.12: Mission-critical architecture chokepoint with corroborated functional dependency; cannot be designed out in current architecture window.
anchors.8: High criticality subsystem input; design-around requires multi-year system redesign.
anchors.4: Moderate criticality; subsystem input with partial alternatives or workarounds.
anchors.0: Generic beneficiary, commodity component, or unproven dependency.

qualified_scarcity_and_switching.description: Effective usable capacity among qualified suppliers, qualification barrier, and customer switching latency.

anchors.14: Single source or semi-monopoly (<2 effective qualified suppliers at ramp); customer switching time >18 months.
anchors.10: 2 to 3 qualified suppliers, but effective usable ramp capacity is severely constrained; switching time 12-18 months.
anchors.5: Multiple qualified alternatives exist, but qualification cycle is 6-12 months.
anchors.0: Abundant qualified capacity, readily available effective substitutes, switching time <6 months, or unproven.

demand_acceleration.description: Multi-year structural demand wave driven by architecture evolution or capex commitments.

anchors.10: Multi-year secular acceleration confirmed by end-customer capex commitments and physical buildout schedules.
anchors.7: Evidenced structural demand wave from tier-1 customers with high confidence.
anchors.3: Moderate industry demand growth without firm architectural lock-in.
anchors.0: Cyclical peak, mature replacement cycle, or unproven demand.

supply_constraint.description: Physical, technical, regulatory, or yield barriers preventing industry supply from expanding rapidly.

anchors.12: Severe physical/tooling lead times (>52 weeks), specialized cleanroom/process know-how, or proprietary IP preventing competitor expansion.
anchors.8: Substantial expansion lead time (24-52 weeks) and high capital intensity limiting fast supply additions.
anchors.4: Moderate lead times (12-24 weeks); capacity expanding in parallel with demand.
anchors.0: Supply elastic or expanding rapidly; unconstrained capacity or unproven constraint.

pricing_power.description: Disclosed contractual price realization, cost-plus pass-through, or willingness-to-pay premium.

anchors.12: Documented contractual price increases, cost-plus indexation, or customer willingness to pay scarcity premium without demand destruction.
anchors.8: Stable pricing power, contractual inflation pass-through, no customer discounting pressure.
anchors.4: Indirect pricing power through product mix shift or high gross margin stability.
anchors.0: Price taker, commodity pricing, high gross margin without pricing mechanism evidence, or unproven.

company_capture.description: Ability of the company's equity holders to capture supply chain economics rather than surrendering value to upstream/downstream partners.

anchors.12: Dominant BOM share capture, low capital leakage, strong balance sheet with no toxic financing dilution.
anchors.8: Strong value capture with manageable capex and non-dilutive balance sheet.
anchors.4: Partial value capture; customer/supplier bargaining pressure or heavy capex burden.
anchors.0: Low value capture; value appropriated by hyperscalers or raw material suppliers; unproven capture.

operating_leverage.description: Conversion of incremental volume and revenue into outsized operating profit and free cash flow.

anchors.10: High fixed-cost absorption resulting in incremental operating margins >40% and accelerating free cash flow.
anchors.7: Demonstrated operating margin expansion with volume scaling.
anchors.3: Moderate operating leverage; linear variable costs dominate.
anchors.0: Negative leverage, diseconomies of scale, heavy unit variable costs, or unproven.

catalyst_and_timing.description: Dated 6-36 month operational catalyst (qualification win, capacity commissioning, volume inflection, platform transition).

anchors.10: Dated 6-18 month verified milestone (e.g. next-gen platform ramp, factory qualification, binding shipment commencement).
anchors.7: Dated 18-36 month verified milestone with corroborated customer timeline.
anchors.3: General roadmap timing without verified contractual/operational milestones.
anchors.0: Distant (>36 months), stale/past, or unproven catalyst.

order_and_commitment_support.description: Firm backlog, take-or-pay agreements, customer prepayments, or capacity reservations.

anchors.8: Disclosed firm non-cancellable backlog, take-or-pay purchase commitments, or customer prepayments/capacity reservations.
anchors.5: Disclosed order book or design win volume commitments with high visibility.
anchors.2: Disclosed non-binding LOI, pilot orders, or qualified pipeline.
anchors.0: Vague TAM references, undisclosed orders, general issuer guidance, or unproven.
